newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU court says Belgium can't stop cartoon TV.
newsitem.headline: EU court says Belgium can't stop cartoon TV.

text.p: European Union countries may not block television broadcasts transmitted from other member states, even if they do not meet European-based programming rules, the European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday.
Under the EU's "television without frontiers" law, EU television channels are required to devote over half their screen time to European programmes "where practicable".

But it is the EU country where the programmer is legally established that decides whether it was practicable to meet the quot a, not the country that receives the broadcast, the court said, confirming an earlier ruling between the Commission and Britain.

Belgium had taken legal action against Paul Denuit, the managing director of the Coditel cable network, for breaking Belgian legislation by broadcasting the London-based Turner Network Television Cartoon Network over its network.

According to court documents, the Belgian Minister for Communications prohibited the TNT Cartoon network because it consists "essentially of programmes produced outside the European (Union) and of commercial advertising".
But the Luxembourg-based court said governments may not unilaterally block broadcasts originating in other member states.
